div.head: Wi 12[b]
div.ab: Gif butwu deoflum geldaþ, sion hio healsfange scyldigo ⁊ ealra æhtan.
Gif butwu deoflum geldaþ, sion hio healsfange scyldigo ⁊ ealra æhtan.
Gif butwu deoflum geldaþ, sion hio healsfange scyldigo ⁊ ealra æhtan.
Wenn beide Götzen opfern, seien sie [beide] Halsfang schuldig und alle [Fahr]habe.
If both sacrifice to idols, let them [both] be liable for healsfang and all their [movable] goods.
If both [of them] make offerings to devils they shall forfeit their healsfangs or all their goods.
If both make offering to devils, they are [both] liable for healsfang or all possessions.

note.seg: ‘und’ = ‘beziehungsweise’ wie Abt 9⁵. Die Ehefrau hat also eigenes Vermögen, wenigstens in Fahrhabe; vgl. Gl eheliches Güterrecht 7
‘and’ = ‘or, as the case may be’, as in Abt 9⁵. The wife therefore has property of her own, at least in movables; cf. Gl eheliches Güterrecht 7
(With Liebermann) and is to be understood as ‘or’ (cf. Abt. cap. 9, etc.).

note.label: healsfang
note.note: The same note as on row 171 (the letter is printed twice).
